task.description: WF-03 Step 1 (CODE-DESIGNER continuation): design POST /api/v1/instances/:id/advance-timer -- request/response contract, targeting semantics, new authz permission wiring, and production-vs-test-only decision, per ISSUE-FIXER's three open questions.

result.summary: Design doc written to lib/letflow/design/iss0389-advance-timer-endpoint.md. Three decisions: (1) targeting -- optional `timer_id` in request body; absent + exactly one pending timer for the instance succeeds (matches the swiftroute scenario fixture's body-less POST step exactly); absent + zero pending timers -> 404; absent + 2+ pending timers -> 400 requiring disambiguation; timer_id given but not-pending/not-found/wrong-instance all fold to the same 404 (INV-5-style). (2) authz -- new permission/endpoint_policy_key atom `:InstancesAdvanceTimer`, fully wired through endpoint_policy_key/2, required_permission/1, and role_allows?/2 (PROCESS_OPERATOR + PLATFORM_ADMIN catch-all only), explicitly NOT following the rebind-pins/reconstruct ad-hoc allowlist pattern since that router's own moduledoc says that shortcut was ruled out going forward -- this follows the AttachmentsManage/AttachmentsRead precedent instead. (3) production route, permission-gated, not simulation-only -- reasoning: fire_timer/2 has no env guard and no precedent exists for env-gated routes in this codebase, the scenario runner issues real HTTP against the real router (not a test-only hook), and there is genuine operational value (ops override for a stuck SLA/escalation timer) comparable to DlqOperate's retry/discard. Design also specifies a new Letflow.Scheduler.resolve_advance_target/3 context function (spec only) so the router never issues Repo.* directly (INV-RT-1), full response/error-status table, the 5 literal edit points across authorization.ex's 4 coordinated sites, 10 mechanically-checkable acceptance criteria, and 2 open questions (recurring-timer special-casing, idempotency-key convention divergence) left explicit rather than silently decided. Flags that test/letflow/simulation/req206_swiftroute_test.exs's existing absence-assertion test (~line 493-506) is now stale and must be deleted/inverted by TEST-DESIGNER, and that the scenario fixture's step 2 should move from via:skip/MINOR to via:api/pass. No implementation code written -- signatures, schemas, and decision tables only.
